title: Daemons can now send traces to Vercel Tracing
description: Vercel Daemons can now send OpenTelemetry traces to Vercel Tracing , allowing you and your agents to inspect background worker operations alongside the rest of your project's traces. Vercel provides each daemon with a Unix socket for receiving OTLP/HTTP traces and sets the socket's path in VERCEL_OTEL_SOCKET_PATH . Upgrading @vercel/otel to version 2.3.0 or later enables automatic trace export for Node.js daemons using the default configuration. The SDK detects this socket and sends the spans your worker records to Vercel. These spans are available through the Vercel CLI , which can search by service name within a project and return JSON for your agents. Learn more in the daemon tracing documentation . Read more

title: Token Pass now includes $150 in tokens for $30/month
description: Vercel Token Pass now includes $150 of tokens per month (up from $80) for the same $30 per team per month. The credit applies to featured open-weight models served through AI Gateway , including Kimi K3, Kimi K3.1 Pro, GLM 5.3, GLM 5.3 Flash, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. Credit resets each billing period with no rollover. When it runs out, requests using standard AI Gateway keys or OIDC tokens fall back to the team's AI Gateway balance, while requests using Token Pass-scoped keys stop with no overage charges. Token Pass is an Early Access add-on for Pro teams, with limited spots and a waitlist when they fill. To connect your coding agent, run vercel token-pass in the Vercel CLI, or use a Token Pass API key if your agent supports AI Gateway. Subscribe to Token Pass in your AI Gateway dashboard . Read more

title: Vercel Security Review no longer requires a linked Vercel project
description: You can now scan code changes for vulnerabilities with Vercel Security Review in GitHub repositories that have not yet been linked to a Vercel project. By default, Security Review covers all unlinked repositories the Vercel GitHub App can access in a connected GitHub account. You can limit coverage to selected connected accounts or individual repositories in Agent settings. Once enabled, each push to a covered repository automatically triggers a review of its code changes. Security Review checks commits directly in repositories with Security Review enabled, without requiring a Vercel project or deployment. When a push creates a deployment for a linked project with Security Review enabled, the review uses the additional project and deployment context. Connect the account in your team’s Git settings , then enable Security Review in Vercel Agent settings . Get started with the Security Review documentation . Read more

title: Vercel Sandbox starts up to 4x faster
description: Vercel Sandbox now initializes up to 4x faster outside the Washington, D.C. ( iad1 ) region when reused image data is served from a regional cache. Initialization now reads cached image data close to where the sandbox runs, avoiding round trips to origin image storage in iad1 on cache hits. Regional caching supports managed and custom images backed by Vercel Container Registry, including snapshots based on those images. In internal end-to-end benchmarks with Vercel Managed Images , startup time fell about 75% in Paris and from about 3.5s to 1.05s in Seoul. Regions closer to origin storage generally see smaller improvements because requests already travel a shorter distance. Learn more in the Vercel Sandbox documentation . Read more
